# godot-3.6.2-api.json — vendored, pinned

Godot's official machine-readable class/member/enum surface for the engine version the ROTA
fixture targets. It is the Godot lane's `Full-API-Dump.json`: the exhaustive spec S1 will walk a
GDScript touch against, and the closure a future coverage checker diffs a backend registry
against. Never hand-authored, only ingested — the same rule Track R applies to Roblox's dump.

## Why this file is not called `extension_api.json`

`extension_api.json` is a **Godot 4** artifact. It is the GDExtension ABI description, produced by
`godot --dump-extension-api`, and that command does not exist before 4.0. ROTA is a **Godot 3.6**
project and cannot be described by it:

- `project.godot` declares `config_version=4` (Godot 3.x; Godot 4 writes `config_version=5`) and
  carries **no `config/features` key at all** — that key is a Godot 4 addition, so the version had
  to be read from the project's own build pin instead of guessed.
- Every vendored `.tscn` header says `format=2` (Godot 3's text-scene format; Godot 4 writes
  `format=3`).
- The upstream repo's release workflow (`.github/workflows/godot.yml`) pins
  `GODOT_VERSION: 3.6.2` and downloads `Godot_v3.6.2-stable_linux_headless.64.zip`. Upstream's
  `readme.md` says "3.6.1" — the CI pin is the newer and more authoritative of the two, and 3.6.1
  vs 3.6.2 is a patch release with no class-surface change.
- The scene graph is Godot-3-shaped throughout: `KinematicBody2D`, `Reference`,
  `VisibilityNotifier2D`, `PoolRealArray` — all renamed or removed in Godot 4.

Vendoring a Godot 4 `extension_api.json` for a Godot 3.6 game would make every dump-membership
answer in S1 wrong in both directions (absent classes reported as unknown, renamed classes
reported as present). So what is vendored is the artifact Godot 3.6 actually publishes for exactly
this purpose: **`api.json`, the GDNative class API dump** — the same file, same role, same
producer, one major version earlier. It is generated by the engine itself
(`godot --gdnative-generate-json-api`) and published per release by the Godot organisation in
`godotengine/godot-headers`; ROTA in fact consumes GDNative through it
(`addons/steam_api/steam_api.gdnlib`).

**Recorded consequence:** when the Godot lane adds a Godot 4 fixture, that fixture needs its own
pinned `extension_api.json` beside this file, and the reader must key the dump off the project's
declared engine version. This file is named for its version for that reason.

## Upstream

- Repo: https://github.com/godotengine/godot-headers (the Godot organisation's own GDNative
  headers repo; one tag per engine release, each carrying the `api.json` generated from that
  release's binary)
- Tag: **`godot-3.6.2-stable`**
- Pinned commit: **`10b5e310edb493de6fcd302a6c27baedec880193`**
- File: `api.json`
- Direct pinned URL:
  `https://raw.githubusercontent.com/godotengine/godot-headers/10b5e310edb493de6fcd302a6c27baedec880193/api.json`
- Retrieved: 2026-08-03
- License: **MIT** (`LICENSE.md` at that commit — "Copyright (c) 2017-2022 Godot Engine
  contributors"), the same license as the engine. Vendoring it is what the repo exists for.

Downloaded, not generated: the official per-release artifact was preferred over running a local
`godot --gdnative-generate-json-api`, so the bytes are the organisation's own and the pin is a
commit anyone can re-fetch.

## Verification

- `sha256`: `8219cab2bf15c89b0a8ada568dae0b587b1032d4853e240b0d0389cfba3b6c02`
  (also recorded machine-readably in `godot-3.6.2-api.json.sha256`, sha256sum style). The upstream
  bytes contain no CR at all, so unlike the Roblox dump there is no CRLF normalization step and
  the recorded hash is over the file exactly as downloaded. Verify it directly with
  `shasum -a 256 -c vendor/extension-api/godot-3.6.2-api.json.sha256` from this package.
- Format: a top-level JSON **array** of class records —
  `{ name, base_class, api_type, singleton, singleton_name, instanciable, is_reference, constants,
  properties, signals, methods, enums }`. At this pin: 690 classes (28 singletons, `api_type` one
  of `core`/`tools`), 9569 methods, 3590 properties, 344 signals, 408 enums.
  Note this is a *different shape* from Godot 4's `extension_api.json`
  (`{ header, builtin_classes, classes, … }`) — another reason the two are separate files rather
  than one path with a version branch.

## Re-vendoring (bumping the pin)

There is deliberately no script for a one-file, one-URL fetch. Resolve the tag
(`gh api repos/godotengine/godot-headers/git/ref/tags/godot-<version>-stable`), `curl` the raw
`api.json` at that commit into `godot-<version>-api.json`, rewrite the `.sha256` sidecar with
`shasum -a 256`, and update the pin block above. A version bump can add/remove/rename classes, so
typecheck the package and run its `report` command over every ladder fixture afterwards.

# godot-4.7-extension_api.json — vendored, pinned

**This is the requisition above, filled.** The section on `godot-3.6.2-api.json` recorded that
"when the Godot lane adds a Godot 4 fixture, that fixture needs its own pinned
`extension_api.json` beside this file, and the reader must key the dump off the project's declared
engine version." `test/fixtures/platformer-3d-godot4` is that fixture (`config_version=5`,
`config/features=PackedStringArray("4.7")`, `format=3` scenes, `Node3D`/`CharacterBody3D`
everywhere), and this file is the artifact it needed. The keying is
`analyze/api-registry.ts`'s `dumpMajorFor` + `loadGodotApiDump(major)`; the two shapes normalize
into one model in `analyze/api-dump.ts`, which is also where the 3.x/4.x deltas are written down.

## Upstream

- Repo: https://github.com/godotengine/godot
- Tag: **`4.7-stable`**
- Pinned commit: **`5b4e0cb0fd279832bbdd69fed5354d4e5ad26f88`** (the engine binary reports its own
  build as `4.7.stable.official.5b4e0cb0f`, and the dump's `header.version_full_name` is
  `Godot Engine v4.7.stable.official`)
- Retrieved: 2026-08-14
- License: **MIT** — the Godot engine's own, `LICENSE.txt` at that tag.

## Generated, not downloaded — and why, unlike the 3.6.2 file

The 3.6.2 pin above is the organisation's own published bytes because Godot 3 ships `api.json` per
release in `godotengine/godot-headers`. Godot 4 has no equivalent to fetch **at this version**:

- the `4.7-stable` release's 35 assets are binaries, export templates and source tarballs — there
  is no `extension_api.json` among them (checked against the release's asset list);
- `godotengine/godot-cpp` — the successor to `godot-headers`, which does check in
  `gdextension/extension_api.json` per release — has no `godot-4.7-stable` tag. Its 4.x tags stop
  at `godot-4.5-stable` (checked against the repo's tag list; a `godot-4.7-stable` ref is a 404).
  Pinning 4.5's copy for a project that declares 4.7 would be the same class of error the whole
  first half of this document is about, only one minor version wide instead of one major.

So the file is generated by the engine itself, which is what the artifact IS — it is the output of
`--dump-extension-api`, not a hand-maintained document — and the chain of custody is the OFFICIAL
BINARY rather than a raw-file URL:

```sh
# 1. the official macOS universal build of 4.7-stable
curl -L -O https://github.com/godotengine/godot/releases/download/4.7-stable/Godot_v4.7-stable_macos.universal.zip
curl -L -O https://github.com/godotengine/godot/releases/download/4.7-stable/SHA512-SUMS.txt
shasum -a 512 Godot_v4.7-stable_macos.universal.zip   # must equal the SHA512-SUMS.txt line:
# 0d5d635e6d78d4c2b1286586ca62af249609c2f70815b35437049f08476714d08b913faaf8c10f37313c932ee24c4f87a829899c84fa248f788fb612b8f79229
unzip -q Godot_v4.7-stable_macos.universal.zip

# 2. the dump, written to the CWD as extension_api.json
mkdir dump && cd dump && ../Godot.app/Contents/MacOS/Godot --headless --dump-extension-api

# 3. vendor it, and rewrite the sidecar
cp extension_api.json <repo>/packages/gd-analyze/vendor/extension-api/godot-4.7-extension_api.json
cd <repo>/packages/gd-analyze/vendor/extension-api
shasum -a 256 godot-4.7-extension_api.json > godot-4.7-extension_api.json.sha256
```

The dump is walked out of `ClassDB`, which is registered identically on every desktop platform, so
the platform above is recorded for reproducibility rather than as a caveat. It is stated because it
is a fact of how these bytes were made, and an unstated one is how a "just regenerate it" note
turns into a diff nobody can explain.

## Verification

- `sha256`: `53d37f85be32b6d10fb2266ca51f6ef0c3a55728acdb7c8301b1458a93c00943`
  (also recorded machine-readably in `godot-4.7-extension_api.json.sha256`, sha256sum style). Like
  the 3.6.2 file these bytes contain no CR at all, so the recorded hash is over the file exactly as
  generated with no normalization step. Re-check it directly with
  `shasum -a 256 -c godot-4.7-extension_api.json.sha256`.
- Format: a top-level JSON **object**. At this pin: `header` (`version_major` 4, `version_minor` 7,
  `version_patch` 0, `version_status` `stable`, `precision` `single`), 1,036 `classes`, 38
  `builtin_classes` (the Variant types — which Godot 3's `api.json` does not enumerate at all), 114
  `utility_functions`, 41 `singletons`, 22 `global_enums`, 11 `global_constants`, 14
  `native_structures`, plus `builtin_class_sizes` / `builtin_class_member_offsets` (ABI data no
  reader in this package opens).
- The lane's own discriminator, asserted rather than assumed: this file declares `Node3D`,
  `CharacterBody3D`, `RigidBody3D`, `Area3D` and `Camera3D`, and declares **no** `Spatial`,
  `KinematicBody2D`, `Reference` or `VisibilityNotifier2D`. The 3.6.2 file is exactly the other way
  round. Neither is a superset of the other, which is why there are two pins and not one.

## The sixteen `@GDScript` functions, which are NOT in this file

`analyze/api-dump.ts` carries a sixteen-name hand list beside this dump's own `utility_functions`.
That is not a memory: Godot 4 splits the receiver-less namespace between `@GlobalScope` (in the
dump, 114 names) and `@GDScript` (compiler intrinsics — `preload`, `assert`, `range`, `len`, …),
and the dump models only the first. The list was taken from the SAME pinned binary:

```sh
mkdir docs && cd docs && ../Godot.app/Contents/MacOS/Godot --headless --doctool .
# → modules/gdscript/doc_classes/@GDScript.xml, its <methods> block
```

`@GDScript.xml` at this pin also confirms the four global CONSTANTS (`INF`, `NAN`, `PI`, `TAU`) are
unchanged from Godot 3, which is why `GDSCRIPT_GLOBAL_CONSTANTS` needs no per-major split.

## Re-vendoring (bumping the pin)

Follow the shell block above with the new tag, rewrite the `.sha256` sidecar, update this section's
version/commit/hash and the format census, then typecheck the package and run its `report` command
over every ladder fixture. If Godot ever begins publishing `extension_api.json` as
a release asset again — or `godot-cpp` resumes tagging — prefer the organisation's own bytes and a
raw-file pin, exactly as the 3.6.2 section does, and say so here.
